stimuli.text: Researchers investigated whether the wording of a question changes what witnesses remember. They recruited 100 adult volunteers who watched a film of a car accident and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition were asked how fast the cars were going when they smashed into each other. Participants in the other condition were asked how fast the cars were going when they contacted each other. The researchers then recorded the speed in kilometers per hour that each participant wrote down.

Researchers investigated whether spreading study sessions out improves long-term retention. They recruited 90 high school students and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition studied a list of 40 words in six ten-minute sessions on six different days. Participants in the other condition studied the same list in a single sixty-minute session. The researchers then recorded the number of words out of 40 that each participant recalled on a test one month later. The results are shown in the table. The difference between the two groups had a p value of 0.01.

rows.group: The group that studied in six short sessions
The group that studied in one long session

stimuli.text: Researchers collected data from 1,200 teenagers. For each one, they recorded the number of hours of social media use per day and score on a depression questionnaire. The correlation between the two measures was r = +0.28.

Researchers investigated whether regular aerobic exercise improves memory in older adults. They recruited 100 adults aged 60 to 75 and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition walked briskly for 40 minutes three times a week for six months. Participants in the other condition did gentle stretching for the same amount of time. The researchers then recorded the number of locations that each participant correctly recalled on a spatial memory test.

Researchers investigated whether agreeing to a small request makes people more likely to agree to a large one. They recruited 120 homeowners and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Homeowners in one condition were first asked to sign a road-safety petition and two weeks later were asked to put a large sign in their garden. Homeowners in the other condition were only asked to put the large sign in their garden. The researchers then recorded the percentage of homeowners in each group who agreed to display the sign.

Researchers investigated whether guided hints help children learn to solve puzzles. They recruited 64 five-year-old children and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Children in one condition solved practice puzzles with hints from an adult that were gradually reduced. Children in the other condition solved the same practice puzzles alone. The researchers then recorded the number of new puzzles out of ten that each child later solved without help.

Researchers investigated whether the color of a drink affects the ability to identify its flavor. They recruited 70 adult volunteers and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition tasted ten fruit drinks whose colors did not match their flavors. Participants in the other condition tasted the same ten drinks with matching colors. The researchers then recorded the number of flavors out of ten that each participant named correctly.

Researchers investigated whether keeping a gratitude journal raises well-being. They recruited 110 adult volunteers and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition wrote down three things they were grateful for every night for a month. Participants in the other condition wrote down three things they had done every night for a month. The researchers then recorded each participant's rating of life satisfaction on a scale from 1 to 10 at the end of the month.

Researchers investigated whether a night without sleep slows reaction time. They recruited 60 adult volunteers and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition stayed awake all night in the laboratory. Participants in the other condition slept for eight hours in the laboratory. The researchers then recorded the average time in milliseconds that each participant took to press a button when a light appeared.

Researchers investigated whether practice quizzes improve memory more than rereading. They recruited 120 university students and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition read a passage once and then took three practice quizzes on it. Participants in the other condition read the same passage four times. The researchers then recorded the percentage of questions that each participant answered correctly on a test one week later.

Researchers investigated whether nausea after a new taste produces an aversion to that taste. They recruited 40 laboratory rats and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Rats in one condition drank sweetened water and were then given an injection that causes mild nausea. Rats in the other condition drank sweetened water and were then given a harmless salt-water injection. The researchers then recorded the volume in milliliters of sweetened water that each rat drank the next day.

Researchers investigated whether children imitate aggressive behavior that they observe. They recruited 72 preschool children and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Children in one condition watched a video of an adult hitting an inflatable doll. Children in the other condition watched a video of an adult playing quietly with other toys. The researchers then recorded the number of times that each child hit the doll during ten minutes of free play.

Researchers investigated whether cognitive-behavioral therapy reduces depression. They recruited 90 adults diagnosed with major depressive disorder and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition received twelve weekly sessions of cognitive-behavioral therapy. Participants in the other condition were placed on a waiting list for twelve weeks and were treated afterward. The researchers then recorded each participant's score on a standard depression questionnaire after twelve weeks.

Read the summary of a hypothetical study, then answer parts A to F.

**Introduction.** Researchers investigated whether the presence of other people slows the reporting of an emergency. They hypothesized that the number of other people present would affect the reporting of an emergency.

**Participants.** The sample was 80 university students, recruited from one city. All participants gave informed consent, were told they could withdraw at any time, and were debriefed afterward. The plan was approved by an institutional review board.

**Method.** The participants were randomly assigned to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition were filling in a form in a room with four other people when smoke began to enter the room. Participants in the other condition were filling in the form alone when smoke began to enter the room. The researchers recorded the time in seconds before each participant left the room to report the smoke.

**Results.** The group that waited with four other people: mean time before reporting (s) = 196. The group that waited alone: mean time before reporting (s) = 58. The difference was statistically significant (p = 0.01).

Use the three hypothetical sources to answer the question: **Does heavy social media use harm the well-being of teenagers?**

**Source A.** A survey of 1,200 teenagers found a correlation of r = +0.28 between hours of social media use per day and scores on a depression questionnaire. Teenagers who reported feeling lonely tended both to use social media more and to have higher depression scores.

**Source B.** In an experiment, 140 university students were randomly assigned either to limit social media use to 30 minutes a day for three weeks or to continue as usual. At the end, the limited group had a mean loneliness score of 38 and the usual-use group a mean of 45 (p = 0.03).

**Source C.** Researchers interviewed 40 teenagers about their experiences online. Many described feeling worse about themselves after viewing images of peers who seemed more attractive or popular; others described feeling supported by online friends who shared their interests.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the defense mechanism of giving a comfortable excuse in place of the real reason for a behavior?

options.why: Correct. Rationalization is the defense mechanism of giving a comfortable excuse in place of the real reason for a behavior.
Displacement is the defense mechanism of shifting an impulse from its real target to a safer one.
Projection is the defense mechanism of seeing one's own unacceptable impulses in other people.
Denial is the defense mechanism of refusing to accept a painful reality.

questions.explanation: Rationalization is the defense mechanism of giving a comfortable excuse in place of the real reason for a behavior.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as a conflict in which a person must choose between two unattractive options?

options.why: Extrinsic motivation is the desire to do something to gain a reward or avoid a punishment.
Intrinsic motivation is the desire to do something for its own sake, because it is enjoyable or satisfying.
An approach-approach conflict is a conflict in which a person must choose between two attractive options.
Correct. An avoidance-avoidance conflict is a conflict in which a person must choose between two unattractive options.

questions.explanation: An avoidance-avoidance conflict is a conflict in which a person must choose between two unattractive options.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes the circadian rhythm?

options.text: The body's roughly 24-hour cycle of wakefulness and sleep
options.why: Correct. This is what the circadian rhythm means.

options.text: The brief, light first stage of sleep, in which a person may have hypnagogic sensations such as falling
options.why: That describes NREM stage 1.

options.text: The deep sleep stage marked by slow delta waves, in which a person is hard to wake
options.why: That describes NREM stage 3.

options.text: The sleep stage with rapid eye movements, vivid dreams, an active brain and relaxed muscles
options.why: That describes REM sleep.

questions.explanation: The circadian rhythm is the body's roughly 24-hour cycle of wakefulness and sleep.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes psychotropic medication?

options.text: The treatment for severe depression in which a brief electric current is passed through the brain of an anesthetized patient
options.why: That describes electroconvulsive therapy.

options.text: The treatment in which repeated magnetic pulses are applied to the surface of the brain to treat depression
options.why: That describes transcranial magnetic stimulation.

options.text: The now-abandoned form of psychosurgery that cut the nerves connecting the frontal lobes to the rest of the brain
options.why: That describes a lobotomy.

options.text: Any drug that acts on the brain to treat the symptoms of a psychological disorder
options.why: Correct. This is what psychotropic medication means.

questions.explanation: Psychotropic medication is any drug that acts on the brain to treat the symptoms of a psychological disorder.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as an attitude that a person holds without being aware of it?

options.why: Prejudice is an unjustified negative attitude toward a group and its members.
A stereotype is a generalized belief about a group of people.
Correct. An implicit attitude is an attitude that a person holds without being aware of it.
Discrimination is unjustified negative behavior toward a group and its members.

questions.explanation: An implicit attitude is an attitude that a person holds without being aware of it.

questions.stem: The group asked about 'smashed' gave higher speed estimates. The difference was statistically significant. Which conclusion is justified?

options.text: The same result would be found in every group of people or animals
options.why: The sample limits how far the result can be generalized.

options.text: The wording of the question and the remembered speed of the cars are related, but no cause can be inferred
options.why: That limit applies to correlational studies; this was an experiment.

options.text: The wording of the question caused the difference in the remembered speed of the cars
options.why: Correct. With random assignment and a manipulated variable, an experiment supports a conclusion about cause and effect.

options.text: The hypothesis has been proved, so the study need not be repeated
options.why: Findings must be replicated; one study does not prove a hypothesis.

questions.explanation: With random assignment and a manipulated variable, an experiment supports a conclusion about cause and effect.

questions.stem: In a crowd of fans, people see the red-shirted fans as one group and the blue-shirted fans as another. Which Gestalt principle explains this?

options.why: Figure and ground is the Gestalt principle that we organize a scene into an object that stands out and its background.
Proximity is the Gestalt principle that we group together objects that are near each other.
Closure is the Gestalt principle that we fill in gaps to see a complete, whole object.
Correct. Similarity is the Gestalt principle that we group together objects that look alike.

questions.explanation: Similarity is the Gestalt principle that we group together objects that look alike.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes primary sex characteristics?

options.text: The body structures, such as ovaries and testes, that make reproduction possible
options.why: Correct. This is what primary sex characteristics means.

options.text: The nonreproductive traits of sexual maturity, such as body hair and a deeper voice
options.why: That describes secondary sex characteristics.

options.text: The natural end of menstruation and of the ability to reproduce, usually around age 50
options.why: That describes menopause.

options.text: The period of sexual maturation, when a person becomes able to reproduce
options.why: That describes puberty.

questions.explanation: Primary sex characteristics is the body structures, such as ovaries and testes, that make reproduction possible.

questions.stem: Which statement about the results is best supported?

options.text: The two groups had the same average result
options.why: The table shows different averages.

options.text: The results prove that every individual in the first group differed from every individual in the second
options.why: The table reports group averages, not individual scores.

options.text: The difference between the groups is probably due to chance
options.why: A p value of 0.01 is below 0.05, so chance is an unlikely explanation.

options.text: The difference between the groups is statistically significant, so it is unlikely to be due to chance
options.why: Correct. A p value below 0.05 means a difference this large would rarely occur by chance alone.

questions.explanation: A p value below 0.05 means a difference this large would rarely occur by chance alone.

questions.stem: Research shows that therapy works better when the client and therapist trust each other and agree on goals. What is this relationship called?

options.why: Correct. The therapeutic alliance is the bond of trust and cooperation between therapist and client.
A meta-analysis is a statistical procedure that combines the results of many studies to reach an overall conclusion.
Cultural humility is a therapist's openness to learning about a client's culture and awareness of the limits of their own view.
Evidence-based practice is the choosing of treatments on the basis of research, clinical skill and the client's own values.

questions.explanation: The therapeutic alliance is the bond of trust and cooperation between therapist and client.

questions.stem: After damage to a small structure below the thalamus, a rat stops eating and no longer regulates its body temperature. Which structure is damaged?

options.why: Correct. The hypothalamus is the structure that regulates hunger, thirst, body temperature and sexual behavior and controls the pituitary gland.
The cerebral cortex is the wrinkled outer layer of the brain, which handles thinking, perception and voluntary movement.
The corpus callosum is the band of fibers that connects the two hemispheres of the brain.
The hippocampus is the structure that forms new explicit memories of facts and events.

questions.explanation: The hypothalamus is the structure that regulates hunger, thirst, body temperature and sexual behavior and controls the pituitary gland.

questions.stem: Researchers find that answers to questions about being talkative, sociable and outgoing all rise and fall together, which suggests a single trait. Which statistical method reveals such clusters?

options.why: Self-efficacy is the belief in one's own ability to succeed at a particular task.
Self-concept is all the thoughts and feelings a person has in answer to the question 'Who am I?'.
Self-esteem is a person's overall feeling of self-worth.
Correct. Factor analysis is the statistical method that finds clusters of related test items, used to identify basic traits.

questions.explanation: Factor analysis is the statistical method that finds clusters of related test items, used to identify basic traits.

questions.stem: A second study of a different pair of measures finds r = −0.48. Which relationship is stronger?

options.text: The relationship with the positive sign, whatever its size
options.why: The sign shows direction, not strength.

options.text: The relationship in the first study, because its coefficient is closer to zero
options.why: A coefficient closer to zero shows a weaker relationship.

options.text: Neither, because relationships with different signs cannot be compared
options.why: Strength can be compared by distance from zero.

options.text: The relationship in the second study, because its coefficient is farther from zero
options.why: Correct. The strength of a correlation is its distance from zero, whatever the sign.

questions.explanation: The strength of a correlation is its distance from zero, whatever the sign.

questions.stem: Immediately after firing, a neuron cannot fire again until it has reset. What is this pause called?

options.why: The action potential is the brief electrical charge that travels down the axon when a neuron fires.
The threshold is the level of stimulation that must be reached for a neuron to fire.
The resting potential is the stable negative charge inside a neuron when it is not firing.
Correct. The refractory period is the brief pause after a neuron fires during which it cannot fire again.

questions.explanation: The refractory period is the brief pause after a neuron fires during which it cannot fire again.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as a sleep disorder in which breathing repeatedly stops during sleep, causing brief awakenings?

options.why: REM sleep behavior disorder is a sleep disorder in which the normal paralysis of REM sleep is missing, so the person acts out dreams.
Correct. Sleep apnea is a sleep disorder in which breathing repeatedly stops during sleep, causing brief awakenings.
Narcolepsy is a sleep disorder with sudden, uncontrollable attacks of sleep, often straight into REM sleep.
Insomnia is a sleep disorder with ongoing difficulty falling asleep or staying asleep.

questions.explanation: Sleep apnea is a sleep disorder in which breathing repeatedly stops during sleep, causing brief awakenings.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the sensory memory of a sound, which lasts three or four seconds?

options.why: Iconic memory is the brief sensory memory of a visual image, which lasts a few tenths of a second.
Working memory is the active processing of information held in mind, combining new input with knowledge from long-term memory.
Short-term memory is the memory store that briefly holds a few items, about seven, before they are stored or forgotten.
Correct. Echoic memory is the sensory memory of a sound, which lasts three or four seconds.

questions.explanation: Echoic memory is the sensory memory of a sound, which lasts three or four seconds.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes altruism?

options.text: A psychologist who studies behavior in the workplace to improve productivity and well-being
options.why: That describes an industrial-organizational psychologist.

options.text: Unselfish concern for the welfare of others
options.why: Correct. This is what altruism means.

options.text: The physical and emotional exhaustion that results from long-term stress at work
options.why: That describes burnout.

options.text: The tendency for a person to be less likely to help when other people are present
options.why: That describes the bystander effect.

questions.explanation: Altruism is unselfish concern for the welfare of others.

questions.stem: Which of the following would be a confounding variable in this study?

options.text: Each one was assigned to a condition at random
options.why: Random assignment reduces confounding; it is not a confound.

options.text: The two groups differed in memory at the end of the study
options.why: That is the dependent variable, the result being measured.

options.text: The walking group met socially after every session, but the stretching group did not
options.why: Correct. It differs between the groups along with the independent variable, so it could explain the results instead.

options.text: One group differed from the other in the type of exercise
options.why: That is the independent variable itself.

questions.explanation: It differs between the groups along with the independent variable, so it could explain the results instead.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the memory to carry out a planned action in the future?

options.why: Correct. Prospective memory is the memory to carry out a planned action in the future.
Procedural memory is the implicit memory of how to perform skills and actions.
Semantic memory is the explicit memory of facts and general knowledge.
Episodic memory is the explicit memory of personally experienced events.

questions.explanation: Prospective memory is the memory to carry out a planned action in the future.

questions.stem: Aaron spends his weekends skydiving and rock climbing. Which form of sensation seeking is this?

options.why: Boredom susceptibility is the form of sensation seeking that involves a strong dislike of repetition and routine.
Disinhibition is the form of sensation seeking that involves a loss of self-restraint, as at wild parties.
Correct. Thrill and adventure seeking is the form of sensation seeking that involves a desire for risky physical activities.
Experience seeking is the form of sensation seeking that involves a desire for new experiences through travel, art and unusual lifestyles.

questions.explanation: Thrill and adventure seeking is the form of sensation seeking that involves a desire for risky physical activities.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the view that development is a gradual, steady process, like a ramp?

options.why: A cross-sectional study is research that compares people of different ages at one point in time.
Correct. Continuous development is the view that development is a gradual, steady process, like a ramp.
Stability and change is the developmental question of which traits stay the same through life and which ones alter.
Nature and nurture is the developmental question of how heredity and experience together shape a person.

questions.explanation: Continuous development is the view that development is a gradual, steady process, like a ramp.

questions.stem: Which of the following is the operational definition of the dependent variable?

options.text: The random assignment of each one to a condition
options.why: This is a control procedure, not a definition of a variable.
This names the variable but does not say how it was measured.

options.text: The percentage of homeowners in each group who agreed to display the sign
options.why: Correct. An operational definition states exactly how a variable is measured.

options.text: Whether a small request came first
options.why: This is the independent variable.

questions.explanation: An operational definition states exactly how a variable is measured.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes relative deprivation?

options.text: The tendency to explain our own behavior by the situation but other people's behavior by their traits
options.why: That describes the actor-observer bias.

options.text: The feeling of being worse off than the people one compares oneself with
options.why: Correct. This is what relative deprivation means.

options.text: The tendency to credit our successes to ourselves and blame our failures on outside factors
options.why: That describes the self-serving bias.

options.text: The habit of explaining bad events as lasting, affecting everything and caused by oneself
options.why: That describes a pessimistic explanatory style.

questions.explanation: Relative deprivation is the feeling of being worse off than the people one compares oneself with.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as a cultural rule about which emotions may be shown, when and to whom?

options.why: An elicitor is an event or stimulus that triggers an emotion.
The facial-feedback hypothesis is the idea that the expression on a person's face can influence the emotion the person feels.
The broaden-and-build theory is the theory that positive emotions widen a person's awareness and help build lasting skills and resources.
Correct. A display rule is a cultural rule about which emotions may be shown, when and to whom.

questions.explanation: A display rule is a cultural rule about which emotions may be shown, when and to whom.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the disorder in which a person has an intense, irrational fear of a particular object or situation?

options.why: Taijin kyofusho is the culture-bound anxiety syndrome, found mainly in Japan, marked by fear of offending or embarrassing others.
Correct. A specific phobia is the disorder in which a person has an intense, irrational fear of a particular object or situation.
Social anxiety disorder is the disorder in which a person has an intense fear of being judged or embarrassed in social situations.
Panic disorder is the disorder in which a person has repeated, unexpected episodes of intense fear with physical symptoms such as chest pain.

questions.explanation: A specific phobia is the disorder in which a person has an intense, irrational fear of a particular object or situation.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes positive punishment?

options.text: The strengthening of a behavior by removing an unpleasant stimulus after it
options.why: That describes negative reinforcement.

options.text: The weakening of a behavior by adding an unpleasant stimulus after it
options.why: Correct. This is what positive punishment means.

options.text: The strengthening of a behavior by adding a pleasant stimulus after it
options.why: That describes positive reinforcement.

options.text: The weakening of a behavior by removing a pleasant stimulus after it
options.why: That describes negative punishment.

questions.explanation: Positive punishment is the weakening of a behavior by adding an unpleasant stimulus after it.

questions.stem: A drug reduces pain and anxiety by acting at the brain's endorphin receptors. Which type of drug is this?

options.why: A stimulant is a drug, such as caffeine or cocaine, that speeds up neural activity and body functions.
Correct. An opioid is a drug, such as heroin, that relieves pain by acting on endorphin receptors and is highly addictive.
A hallucinogen is a drug, such as marijuana, that distorts perception and can cause sensory experiences without sensory input.
A depressant is a drug, such as alcohol, that slows neural activity and body functions.

questions.explanation: An opioid is a drug, such as heroin, that relieves pain by acting on endorphin receptors and is highly addictive.

questions.stem: Scores on a university entrance test correlate strongly with students' later grades. Which quality does the test have?

options.why: Test-retest reliability is the consistency of scores when the same people take the same test twice.
Correct. Predictive validity is the extent to which test scores forecast the future performance they are meant to predict.
Standardization is the giving and scoring of a test in the same way for everyone, and the comparison of scores with a pretested group.
Split-half reliability is the consistency of scores between two halves of the same test.

questions.explanation: Predictive validity is the extent to which test scores forecast the future performance they are meant to predict.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the improved recall that occurs in the same place where the information was learned?

options.why: Mood-congruent memory is the tendency to recall memories that match one's current mood.
Correct. Context-dependent memory is the improved recall that occurs in the same place where the information was learned.
A retrieval cue is a stimulus that helps bring a memory to mind.
Recognition is the identification of previously learned information when it is presented, as in a multiple-choice question.

questions.explanation: Context-dependent memory is the improved recall that occurs in the same place where the information was learned.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes a reuptake inhibitor?

options.text: The need for larger doses of a drug to get the same effect after repeated use
options.why: That describes tolerance.

options.text: A drug that keeps a neurotransmitter in the synapse longer by blocking its reabsorption
options.why: Correct. This is what a reuptake inhibitor means.

options.text: A drug that increases the action of a neurotransmitter, for example by mimicking it
options.why: That describes an agonist.

options.text: The unpleasant physical and psychological symptoms that follow stopping an addictive drug
options.why: That describes withdrawal.

questions.explanation: A reuptake inhibitor is a drug that keeps a neurotransmitter in the synapse longer by blocking its reabsorption.

questions.stem: Asked about his future, Cole shrugs; he has not thought about it and does not care to. Which identity status is this?

options.why: Correct. Identity diffusion is the identity status of a person who has neither explored options nor made a commitment.
Identity achievement is the identity status of a person who has explored options and made a commitment.
Identity moratorium is the identity status of a person who is actively exploring options but has not yet made a commitment.
Identity foreclosure is the identity status of a person who has made a commitment without exploring options.

questions.explanation: Identity diffusion is the identity status of a person who has neither explored options nor made a commitment.

questions.stem: Grandpa tells detailed stories about his wedding day and his first job. Which kind of memory is he drawing on?

options.why: Maintenance rehearsal is the repeating of information over and over to keep it in short-term memory.
Highly superior autobiographical memory is the rare ability to recall almost every day of one's life in detail.
Correct. Autobiographical memory is the memory of the events of one's own life.
Elaborative rehearsal is the linking of new information to existing knowledge and meaning to store it in long-term memory.

questions.explanation: Autobiographical memory is the memory of the events of one's own life.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes the behavioral perspective?

options.text: The view that disorders result from social and cultural factors, such as poverty and discrimination
options.why: That describes the sociocultural perspective.

options.text: The view that disorders result from learned associations and reinforcement
options.why: Correct. This is what the behavioral perspective means.

options.text: The view that disorders involve behaviors that once helped survival but are now harmful
options.why: That describes the evolutionary perspective.

options.text: The view that disorders result from unconscious conflicts, often rooted in childhood
options.why: That describes the psychodynamic perspective.

questions.explanation: The behavioral perspective is the view that disorders result from learned associations and reinforcement.

questions.stem: After an hour in a bakery, the workers no longer notice the smell of bread. This best illustrates which of the following?

options.why: The just-noticeable difference is the smallest difference between two stimuli that a person can detect half of the time.
Correct. Sensory adaptation is the reduced sensitivity that follows constant, unchanging stimulation.
Weber's law is the principle that two stimuli must differ by a constant proportion, not a constant amount, to be noticed.
The absolute threshold is the weakest level of a stimulus that a person can detect half of the time.

questions.explanation: Sensory adaptation is the reduced sensitivity that follows constant, unchanging stimulation.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes social loafing?

options.text: The tendency for people to put in less effort when working in a group than when working alone
options.why: Correct. This is what social loafing means.

options.text: The reduced sense of personal duty to act when other people are present
options.why: That describes diffusion of responsibility.

options.text: The kind of thinking in which the desire for agreement in a group overrides a realistic evaluation of alternatives
options.why: That describes groupthink.

options.text: The loss of self-awareness and self-restraint in group situations that provide arousal and anonymity
options.why: That describes deindividuation.

questions.explanation: Social loafing is the tendency for people to put in less effort when working in a group than when working alone.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes continuous reinforcement?

options.text: The schedule in which the behavior is reinforced after an unpredictable number of responses
options.why: That describes a variable-ratio schedule.

options.text: The schedule in which the behavior is reinforced every time it occurs
options.why: Correct. This is what continuous reinforcement means.

options.text: The schedule in which the behavior is reinforced after a set number of responses
options.why: That describes a fixed-ratio schedule.

options.text: The schedule in which the first response after a set amount of time is reinforced
options.why: That describes a fixed-interval schedule.

questions.explanation: Continuous reinforcement is the schedule in which the behavior is reinforced every time it occurs.

questions.stem: Freud argued that slips of the tongue reveal wishes that people do not know they have. Where did he believe these wishes are held?

options.why: A projective test is a personality test, such as an inkblot test, that asks people to interpret unclear images in order to reveal hidden feelings.
Unconditional positive regard is the attitude of total acceptance toward another person, whatever they say or do.
Correct. The unconscious is in psychodynamic theory, the store of thoughts, wishes and memories that a person is not aware of but that still influences behavior.
The self-actualizing tendency is in humanistic theory, the inborn drive of people to grow and fulfill their potential.

questions.explanation: The unconscious is in psychodynamic theory, the store of thoughts, wishes and memories that a person is not aware of but that still influences behavior.

questions.stem: Athletes perform poorly when they are either too relaxed or too anxious, and best when moderately excited. This best illustrates which of the following?

options.why: Self-determination theory is the theory that people are motivated by needs for competence, autonomy and relatedness, either from within or from outside.
Drive-reduction theory is the theory that a physical need creates a state of tension that motivates behavior to reduce it.
Correct. The Yerkes-Dodson law is the principle that performance is best at a moderate level of arousal.
Homeostasis is the body's tendency to keep its internal state, such as temperature, steady.

questions.explanation: The Yerkes-Dodson law is the principle that performance is best at a moderate level of arousal.

questions.stem: In the strange situation, a toddler shows little reaction when her mother leaves and turns away when she returns. Which attachment style is this?

options.why: Correct. Avoidant attachment is the insecure attachment style in which a child seems indifferent when the caregiver leaves and ignores the caregiver on return.
Separation anxiety is the distress that infants show when a familiar caregiver leaves, which peaks around 13 months.
Secure attachment is the attachment style in which a child uses the caregiver as a safe base, is upset when the caregiver leaves and is comforted on return.
Disorganized attachment is the insecure attachment style in which a child shows confused, contradictory behavior toward the caregiver.

questions.explanation: Avoidant attachment is the insecure attachment style in which a child seems indifferent when the caregiver leaves and ignores the caregiver on return.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes the serial position effect?

options.text: The finding that study spread over time produces better long-term memory than study crammed together
options.why: That describes the spacing effect.

options.text: The tendency to remember the first and last items in a list better than the middle ones
options.why: Correct. This is what the serial position effect means.

options.text: The tendency to remember the first items in a list well
options.why: That describes the primacy effect.

options.text: The tendency to remember the last items in a list well
options.why: That describes the recency effect.

questions.explanation: The serial position effect is the tendency to remember the first and last items in a list better than the middle ones.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes a percentile rank?

options.text: The percentage of scores in a distribution that fall at or below a given score
options.why: Correct. This is what a percentile rank means.

options.text: The difference between the highest and lowest scores
options.why: That describes the range.

options.text: A distribution with a few extremely low scores, which pull the mean below the median
options.why: That describes a negative skew.

options.text: The arithmetic average of a set of scores
options.why: That describes the mean.

questions.explanation: A percentile rank is the percentage of scores in a distribution that fall at or below a given score.

questions.stem: What is the independent variable in this study?

options.why: This is a procedure for forming the groups, not a variable.
This was measured, not manipulated: it is the dependent variable.

options.text: The number of participants in the study
options.why: This is the sample size, not a variable the researchers changed.
Correct. The independent variable is the factor the researchers changed between the two conditions.

questions.explanation: The independent variable is the factor the researchers changed between the two conditions.

questions.stem: Red light and blue light differ in color. Which property of the light waves differs?

options.why: Frequency is the number of sound waves per second, which determines pitch.
Correct. Wavelength is the distance from one wave peak to the next, which determines the hue of light.
The cochlea is the coiled, fluid-filled tube in the inner ear where sound waves become neural impulses.
Amplitude is the height of a sound wave, which determines loudness.

questions.explanation: Wavelength is the distance from one wave peak to the next, which determines the hue of light.

questions.stem: After the study, the researchers explained its full purpose to every participant and answered their questions. What is this called?

options.why: Replication is repeating a study.
Consent is obtained before the study.
A placebo is an inactive treatment.
Correct. Debriefing explains the study, including any deception, once it is over.

questions.explanation: Debriefing explains the study, including any deception, once it is over.

questions.stem: 'Because I said so' is the only explanation that Tara's parents ever give for their many strict rules. Which parenting style is this?

options.why: Temperament is a person's characteristic emotional reactivity and intensity, which appears early in life.
Authoritative parenting is the parenting style that sets firm rules but explains them, listens and is warm.
Permissive parenting is the parenting style that makes few demands and sets few limits.
Correct. Authoritarian parenting is the parenting style that sets strict rules and expects obedience, with little warmth or discussion.

questions.explanation: Authoritarian parenting is the parenting style that sets strict rules and expects obedience, with little warmth or discussion.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the use of the principles of conditioning to increase helpful behaviors and reduce harmful ones?

options.why: A token economy is the behavioral system in which people earn tokens for desired behavior and exchange them for rewards.
Biofeedback is the technique of using electronic monitoring to show a person their body's signals so that they can learn to control them.
Aversion therapy is the behavioral treatment that pairs an unwanted behavior with an unpleasant stimulus.
Correct. Applied behavior analysis is the use of the principles of conditioning to increase helpful behaviors and reduce harmful ones.

questions.explanation: Applied behavior analysis is the use of the principles of conditioning to increase helpful behaviors and reduce harmful ones.

questions.stem: A researcher claims that dreams have no hidden meaning; the cortex simply builds a story out of random signals from the brainstem. Which theory is this?

options.why: Correct. The activation-synthesis theory is the theory that dreams are the brain's attempt to make sense of random neural activity during sleep.
Memory consolidation is the strengthening of memories that takes place during sleep.
Restoration is the repair of body and brain tissue that takes place during sleep.
The consolidation theory is the theory that dreaming helps sort and strengthen the day's memories.

questions.explanation: The activation-synthesis theory is the theory that dreams are the brain's attempt to make sense of random neural activity during sleep.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the group of personality disorders marked by dramatic, emotional or erratic behavior: antisocial, borderline, histrionic and narcissistic?

options.why: Cluster C is the group of personality disorders marked by anxious or fearful behavior: avoidant, dependent and obsessive-compulsive.
A personality disorder is a lasting, rigid pattern of behavior and inner experience that differs from cultural expectations and impairs functioning.
Cluster A is the group of personality disorders marked by odd or eccentric behavior: paranoid, schizoid and schizotypal.
Correct. Cluster B is the group of personality disorders marked by dramatic, emotional or erratic behavior: antisocial, borderline, histrionic and narcissistic.

questions.explanation: Cluster B is the group of personality disorders marked by dramatic, emotional or erratic behavior: antisocial, borderline, histrionic and narcissistic.

questions.stem: Another research team repeats this study with new subjects and obtains the same result. What is this called?

options.why: That is explaining the study to participants afterward.
Correct. Replication is repeating a study to see whether the finding holds.
That is how subjects are placed in conditions.
That is an in-depth study of one individual.

questions.explanation: Replication is repeating a study to see whether the finding holds.

questions.stem: The smell of sunscreen instantly brings back a vivid memory of a childhood holiday. Which sense has this close link to emotion and memory areas?

options.why: A supertaster is a person with more taste receptors than average, who experiences tastes more intensely.
Correct. Olfaction is the sense of smell, the only sense that does not pass through the thalamus first.
A pheromone is a chemical signal released by one member of a species that affects the behavior of others.
Gustation is the sense of taste, which detects sweet, sour, salty, bitter, umami and oleogustus.

questions.explanation: Olfaction is the sense of smell, the only sense that does not pass through the thalamus first.

questions.stem: Dee cannot stop thinking that her hands are covered in germs. This repeated, unwanted thought is which of the following?

options.why: Dissociative identity disorder is the disorder in which a person shows two or more distinct personalities that take control at different times.
Correct. An obsession is an unwanted thought or urge that keeps returning and causes anxiety.
Dissociative amnesia is the disorder in which a person cannot remember important personal information, usually after trauma and with no physical cause, sometimes with travel away from home (fugue).
Posttraumatic stress disorder is the disorder in which a person has flashbacks, nightmares, watchfulness and avoidance for more than a month after a terrifying event.

questions.explanation: An obsession is an unwanted thought or urge that keeps returning and causes anxiety.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the encoding of information, such as space, time and frequency, without conscious effort?

options.why: Implicit memory is the memory of skills and learned associations that is retained without conscious recall.
Phonemic encoding is the encoding of a word based on its sound.
Structural encoding is the shallow encoding of a word based on its appearance.
Correct. Automatic processing is the encoding of information, such as space, time and frequency, without conscious effort.

questions.explanation: Automatic processing is the encoding of information, such as space, time and frequency, without conscious effort.

questions.stem: Before taking part, each participant was told what the study would involve and what the risks were, and then agreed to take part. Which ethical guideline does this meet?

options.why: Correct. Participants must agree to take part after being told what the study involves.
Confidentiality is keeping participants' data private.
Debriefing happens after the study.
That is a research procedure, not an ethical guideline.

questions.explanation: Participants must agree to take part after being told what the study involves.

questions.stem: A hormone released during childbirth and nursing strengthens the bond between parent and infant. Which hormone is this?

options.why: Ghrelin is the hormone released by an empty stomach that increases hunger.
Adrenaline is the hormone released by the adrenal glands that raises heart rate and energy during stress.
Correct. Oxytocin is the hormone that promotes bonding, trust and social attachment.
Leptin is the hormone released by fat cells that signals fullness and reduces hunger.

questions.explanation: Oxytocin is the hormone that promotes bonding, trust and social attachment.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes an eclectic approach?

options.text: The presence of two or more disorders in the same person at the same time
options.why: That describes comorbidity.

options.text: The view that disorders result from the interaction of biological, psychological and social factors
options.why: That describes the biopsychosocial model.

options.text: The view that a disorder develops when an inherited vulnerability is triggered by stressful experience
options.why: That describes the diathesis-stress model.

options.text: The use of techniques from several types of therapy, depending on the client's problem
options.why: Correct. This is what an eclectic approach means.

questions.explanation: An eclectic approach is the use of techniques from several types of therapy, depending on the client's problem.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as Erikson's stage in young adulthood, in which people seek close, lasting relationships?

options.why: Identity versus role confusion is Erikson's stage in adolescence, in which teenagers work out who they are.
Correct. Intimacy versus isolation is Erikson's stage in young adulthood, in which people seek close, lasting relationships.
Integrity versus despair is Erikson's stage in late adulthood, in which people look back on life with satisfaction or regret.
Generativity versus stagnation is Erikson's stage in middle adulthood, in which people seek to contribute to the world through family and work.

questions.explanation: Intimacy versus isolation is Erikson's stage in young adulthood, in which people seek close, lasting relationships.

questions.stem: After weeks of deep depression, Mia goes a week with almost no sleep, talks nonstop, spends all her savings and believes she has special powers, and is taken to hospital. Which disorder does this suggest?

options.why: Persistent depressive disorder is the disorder in which a person has a mildly depressed mood on most days for at least two years.
Correct. Bipolar I disorder is the disorder in which a person has full manic episodes, usually alternating with depression.
Major depressive disorder is the disorder in which a person has at least two weeks of depressed mood or loss of interest, with other symptoms such as changes in sleep and appetite.
Bipolar II disorder is the disorder in which a person alternates between depression and a milder form of mania called hypomania.

questions.explanation: Bipolar I disorder is the disorder in which a person has full manic episodes, usually alternating with depression.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as in ecological systems theory, the groups that have direct contact with the child, such as family and school?

options.why: The macrosystem is in ecological systems theory, the cultural values, laws and customs that surround a child.
The chronosystem is in ecological systems theory, the life stage and historical events that affect a child.
The exosystem is in ecological systems theory, the settings that affect a child indirectly, such as a parent's workplace.
Correct. The microsystem is in ecological systems theory, the groups that have direct contact with the child, such as family and school.

questions.explanation: The microsystem is in ecological systems theory, the groups that have direct contact with the child, such as family and school.

questions.stem: A researcher flips a coin to decide whether each volunteer goes into the treatment group or the control group. Which procedure is this?

options.why: Correct. Random assignment is the placing of participants in experimental conditions by chance.
Generalizability is the extent to which the findings of a study apply to people beyond the sample.
Sampling bias is a flaw in selecting participants that makes the sample unlike the population.
A representative sample is a sample whose characteristics match those of the population it is drawn from.

questions.explanation: Random assignment is the placing of participants in experimental conditions by chance.

questions.stem: A school celebrates the languages, foods and holidays of all the cultures among its students. Which view does this reflect?

options.why: Obedience is the following of the direct commands of an authority figure.
Correct. Multiculturalism is the view that the different cultural groups in a society should be valued and should keep their identities.
Collectivism is the cultural pattern that gives priority to the goals of the group and defines identity by group membership.
A superordinate goal is a shared goal that can be reached only if groups cooperate, which reduces conflict between them.

questions.explanation: Multiculturalism is the view that the different cultural groups in a society should be valued and should keep their identities.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as Piaget's stage from birth to about age 2, in which infants know the world through senses and actions?

options.why: Correct. The sensorimotor stage is Piaget's stage from birth to about age 2, in which infants know the world through senses and actions.
The concrete operational stage is Piaget's stage from about age 7 to 11, in which children think logically about real objects and events.
The formal operational stage is Piaget's stage from about age 12 on, in which people can reason about abstract and hypothetical ideas.
The preoperational stage is Piaget's stage from about age 2 to 7, in which children use words and images but cannot yet reason logically.

questions.explanation: The sensorimotor stage is Piaget's stage from birth to about age 2, in which infants know the world through senses and actions.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as a memory aid that uses vivid images or organizing tricks?

options.why: Correct. A mnemonic device is a memory aid that uses vivid images or organizing tricks.
Distributed practice is study that is spread out over several sessions.
The method of loci is the mnemonic of imagining items placed at locations along a familiar route.
Chunking is the organizing of items into familiar, manageable units.

questions.explanation: A mnemonic device is a memory aid that uses vivid images or organizing tricks.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes the axon?

options.text: The endings of the axon that release neurotransmitters
options.why: That describes the axon terminals.

options.text: The tiny gap between the sending neuron and the receiving neuron
options.why: That describes the synapse.

options.text: The fatty layer around some axons that speeds up neural impulses
options.why: That describes the myelin sheath.

options.text: The long fiber that carries the neural impulse away from the cell body toward other cells
options.why: Correct. This is what the axon means.

questions.explanation: The axon is the long fiber that carries the neural impulse away from the cell body toward other cells.

questions.stem: In Pavlov's experiments, dogs salivated to food, and later to a tone that had been paired with food. The food was which of the following?

options.why: The conditioned stimulus is in classical conditioning, the originally neutral stimulus that triggers a response after being paired with another stimulus.
The conditioned response is in classical conditioning, the learned response to a previously neutral stimulus.
Correct. The unconditioned stimulus is in classical conditioning, the stimulus that triggers a response naturally, without learning.
The unconditioned response is in classical conditioning, the natural, unlearned response to a stimulus.

questions.explanation: The unconditioned stimulus is in classical conditioning, the stimulus that triggers a response naturally, without learning.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the inability to see that an object can be used for something other than its usual purpose?

options.why: A mental set is the tendency to approach a problem in a way that has worked before, even when it no longer works.
Convergent thinking is thinking that narrows the possibilities down to the single best answer.
An algorithm is a step-by-step procedure that guarantees a solution.
Correct. Functional fixedness is the inability to see that an object can be used for something other than its usual purpose.

questions.explanation: Functional fixedness is the inability to see that an object can be used for something other than its usual purpose.

questions.stem: A therapist stops using a technique when she sees that it is making her client worse. Which ethical principle is she following?

options.text: Respect for people's rights and dignity
options.why: Respect for people's rights and dignity is the ethical principle that psychologists must protect privacy, confidentiality and the right of people to make their own choices.
Fidelity is the ethical principle that psychologists must be trustworthy and keep their professional promises.
Integrity is the ethical principle that psychologists must be honest and accurate.
Correct. Nonmaleficence is the ethical principle that psychologists must avoid doing harm.

questions.explanation: Nonmaleficence is the ethical principle that psychologists must avoid doing harm.

questions.stem: After the study behind his favorite diet is shown to be fraudulent, Raj still insists that the diet works. This best illustrates which of the following?

options.why: Correct. Belief perseverance is the tendency to hold on to a belief even after the evidence for it has been discredited.
Confirmation bias is the tendency to search for and favor information that supports what one already believes.
In-group bias is the tendency to favor the members of one's own group.
Out-group homogeneity bias is the tendency to see the members of other groups as all alike.

questions.explanation: Belief perseverance is the tendency to hold on to a belief even after the evidence for it has been discredited.

questions.stem: Ben is tormented by constant worry and feels miserable most of the day. Which criterion for a psychological disorder does this meet?

options.why: The DSM is the American Psychiatric Association's manual for classifying and diagnosing psychological disorders.
Stigma is the negative attitudes and discrimination directed at people who have a psychological disorder.
Dysfunction is the criterion for a disorder that the behavior interferes with daily life, such as work and relationships.
Correct. Distress is the criterion for a disorder that the behavior causes suffering to the person.

questions.explanation: Distress is the criterion for a disorder that the behavior causes suffering to the person.

questions.stem: After the study, the researchers explained its full purpose to every participant and answered their questions. What is this called?

options.why: Consent is obtained before the study.
Correct. Debriefing explains the study, including any deception, once it is over.
A placebo is an inactive treatment.
Replication is repeating a study.

questions.explanation: Debriefing explains the study, including any deception, once it is over.

questions.stem: All of the subjects in this study were drawn from one group: 40 laboratory rats. What does this most limit?

options.text: Whether the dependent variable was operationally defined
options.why: The measure was clearly defined.

options.text: Whether a cause-and-effect conclusion can be drawn
options.why: Random assignment, not the sample, allows the causal conclusion.

options.text: How far the findings can be generalized to other populations
options.why: Correct. A sample that does not represent the wider population limits generalizability.

options.text: Whether the study had a control group
options.why: The study had a comparison condition.

questions.explanation: A sample that does not represent the wider population limits generalizability.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the category of character strengths that includes teamwork, fairness and leadership?

options.why: Correct. Justice is the category of character strengths that includes teamwork, fairness and leadership.
Courage is the category of character strengths that includes bravery, honesty and perseverance.
Humanity is the category of character strengths that includes love, kindness and social intelligence.
Wisdom is the category of character strengths that includes creativity, curiosity and love of learning.

questions.explanation: Justice is the category of character strengths that includes teamwork, fairness and leadership.

questions.stem: Another research team repeats this study with new subjects and obtains the same result. What is this called?

options.why: That is how subjects are placed in conditions.
That is explaining the study to participants afterward.
Correct. Replication is repeating a study to see whether the finding holds.
That is an in-depth study of one individual.

questions.explanation: Replication is repeating a study to see whether the finding holds.

questions.stem: A man with strong aggressive urges becomes a successful boxer. Which defense mechanism is this?

options.why: Reaction formation is the defense mechanism of acting in the opposite way to one's unacceptable impulses.
Regression is the defense mechanism of retreating to behavior from an earlier stage of development.
Repression is the defense mechanism of pushing anxiety-arousing thoughts and memories out of awareness.
Correct. Sublimation is the defense mechanism of turning unacceptable impulses into socially valued activities.

questions.explanation: Sublimation is the defense mechanism of turning unacceptable impulses into socially valued activities.

questions.stem: Scores on a test are normally distributed with a mean of 500 and a standard deviation of 15. About what percentage of scores are above 530?

options.why: Correct. 95% lie within two standard deviations, leaving 5% outside, half of which (2.5%) is above.
This does not match the 68–95 rule for a normal distribution.
This does not match the 68–95 rule for a normal distribution.
This does not match the 68–95 rule for a normal distribution.

questions.explanation: 95% lie within two standard deviations, leaving 5% outside, half of which (2.5%) is above. (485 and 515 are one standard deviation from the mean; 470 and 530 are two.)

questions.stem: What is the dependent variable in this study?

options.why: A hypothesis is a prediction, not a variable.

options.text: The condition to which each one was assigned
options.why: This describes the independent variable.
This was manipulated by the researchers: it is the independent variable.
Correct. The dependent variable is the outcome that the researchers measured.

questions.explanation: The dependent variable is the outcome that the researchers measured.

questions.title: Article analysis: a study of the reporting of an emergency

parts.prompt: Identify the research method used in the study.

rubric.criterion: Identifies the method as an experiment.
rubric.example: The study is an experiment: the researchers manipulated a variable and randomly assigned the subjects to conditions.

parts.prompt: State the operational definition of the reporting of an emergency.

rubric.criterion: States how the variable was measured in this study.
rubric.example: The reporting of an emergency was defined as the time in seconds before each participant left the room to report the smoke.

parts.prompt: Describe the meaning of the difference between the two group averages.

rubric.criterion: Accurately describes which group scored higher or lower and what that means for the variable measured.
rubric.example: The participants who were with other people took longer to report the smoke. On average, the value was 196 for the group that waited with four other people and 58 for the group that waited alone, and a p value of 0.01 means a difference this large is unlikely to be due to chance.

parts.prompt: Identify at least one ethical guideline applied by the researchers.

rubric.criterion: Identifies an ethical guideline that the summary shows was followed.
rubric.example: Informed consent: participants agreed to take part after being told about the study. (Also acceptable: debriefing; the right to withdraw; approval by an institutional review board.)

parts.prompt: Explain the extent to which the research findings may or may not be generalizable, using specific and relevant evidence from the study.

rubric.criterion: Explains a limit (or strength) of generalizability with reference to the sample.
rubric.example: The sample was 80 university students from one city, so the findings may not apply to people of other ages, cultures or backgrounds. Because the sample was not randomly selected from a wider population, it may not be representative.

parts.prompt: Explain how at least one of the research findings supports or refutes the researchers' hypothesis.

rubric.criterion: Uses a specific finding from the study as evidence.
rubric.example: The participants who were with other people took longer to report the smoke. (196 compared with 58).

rubric.criterion: Explains how the finding supports the hypothesis, using a psychological concept.
rubric.example: This supports the hypothesis that the number of other people present affects the reporting of an emergency. Because subjects were randomly assigned, the difference can be attributed to the number of other people present. The finding illustrates the bystander effect and diffusion of responsibility: people feel less personal duty to act when others are present.

questions.title: Evidence-based question: Does heavy social media use harm the well-being of teenagers?

parts.prompt: Propose a specific and defensible claim, based in psychological science, that responds to the question.

rubric.criterion: States a claim that answers the question and can be supported by the sources.
rubric.example: Heavy social media use can harm teenagers' well-being, especially when it leads them to compare themselves with others.

parts.prompt: (i) Support your claim using at least one piece of specific and relevant evidence from one of the sources. (ii) Explain how the evidence supports your claim, using a psychological perspective, theory, concept or research finding learned in AP Psychology.

rubric.criterion: Uses specific, relevant evidence from one source and names the source.
rubric.example: In Source B, students who limited social media to 30 minutes a day had lower loneliness scores (38) than students who continued as usual (45).

rubric.criterion: Explains how the evidence supports the claim.
rubric.example: This supports the claim because the study was an experiment with random assignment, so reducing social media use can be said to have caused the lower loneliness. Less time online leaves more time for face-to-face contact, which supports well-being.

rubric.criterion: Correctly applies a psychological concept in the explanation.
rubric.example: The concept must be named and applied correctly, as in the model explanation.

parts.prompt: (i) Support your claim using an additional piece of specific and relevant evidence from a different source. (ii) Explain how this evidence supports your claim, using a different psychological perspective, theory, concept or research finding.

rubric.criterion: Uses specific, relevant evidence from a different source and names the source.
rubric.example: In Source C, many teenagers said they felt worse about themselves after viewing images of peers who seemed more attractive or popular.

rubric.criterion: Explains how the evidence supports the claim.
rubric.example: This supports the claim through upward social comparison and relative deprivation: comparing oneself with people who seem better off lowers self-esteem and satisfaction.

rubric.criterion: Correctly applies a different psychological concept from the one used in part B.
rubric.example: The concept must differ from the one used in part B and be applied correctly.
